original_question: Determine whether there exist an integer t and an absolute constant c>0 such that for every n, the maximum size g_{K_{t,t}}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] whose pairwise intersections contain a copy of K_{t,t} satisfies g_{K_{t,t}}(n) <= (1-c) 2^{C(n,2)-1}.
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Some problems on intersecting families of graphs"), Conjecture 4.6.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It has the right graph parameter g_{K_{t,t}}(n), the right quantifier pattern (existence of a single integer t and a single absolute constant c>0), the right extremal setting (families of graphs on [n] whose pairwise intersections contain K_{t,t}), and the right upper bound, namely a constant-factor improvement over the trivial bound 2^{\binom{n}{2}-1}. This is essentially Conjecture 4.6.
missing_details: The paper first defines [n]={1,2,...,n} and works with families of labelled graphs on the common vertex set [n].
The relevant notion is H-intersecting: for every pair G_1,G_2 in the family, the edgewise intersection G_1∩G_2 must contain a copy of H.
The notation g_H(n) is defined explicitly as g_H(n):=max{|F| : F is an H-intersecting family of graphs on [n]}.
The quantifiers are global: one seeks a single t in N and a single absolute constant c>0 that work simultaneously for every n in N.
The paper states this as a specific conjecture, not as a broader classification problem.
Nearby context notes that the especially interesting special case is t=2, i.e. H=C_4=K_{2,2}, since proving that case would imply the others.
refined_question: Does there exist an integer t>=1 and an absolute constant c>0 such that, for every n>=1, every K_{t,t}-intersecting family F of labelled graphs on the vertex set [n]={1,2,...,n} satisfies |F| <= (1-c)2^{\binom{n}{2}-1}? Here K_{t,t}-intersecting means that G_1∩G_2 contains a copy of K_{t,t} for every G_1,G_2 in F.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the paper’s notation g_H(n):=max{|F| : F is an H-intersecting family of graphs on [n]}, does there exist t in N and an absolute constant c>0 such that g_{K_{t,t}}(n) <= (1-c)2^{\binom{n}{2}-1} for all n in N?
justification: Section 4 first introduces the notion of an H-intersecting family and defines g_H(n). Conjecture 4.6 then states essentially your draft verbatim, with H=K_{t,t}. The surrounding discussion shows that this conjecture is intended as a much weaker bipartite substitute for the Alon–Spencer conjecture about P_3-intersecting families, and it explicitly singles out t=2 (that is, C_4) as the most interesting case. The nearby stronger statements (Proposition 4.2, Conjectures 4.3 and 4.4) are chromatic-number variants, not equivalent reformulations of Conjecture 4.6, so the only paper-faithful alternate formulation is the one obtained by unpacking the definition of g_H(n).
